title: Closest Fair Integer
summary: Given a positive integer n, find the smallest fair integer greater than or equal to n.
statement: Given a positive integer n, find the smallest fair integer greater than or equal to n. An integer k is fair if it has an equal number of even and odd digits.
constraints: n is a positive integer at most 10^9.
A fair integer contains equal counts of even and odd decimal digits; zero is an even digit.
Return the smallest fair integer greater than or equal to n.
hints: A fair number must have an even number of digits.
If n has odd length, construct the smallest fair number of the next length; otherwise scan until the digit counts balance.
Count digit parities, handling the odd-length jump directly, and stop at the first balanced candidate.
The scan tests candidates in increasing order, while the constructed next-length value is lexicographically smallest with half odd and half even digits, so the first result is minimal.
editorial: The scan tests candidates in increasing order, while the constructed next-length value is lexicographically smallest with half odd and half even digits, so the first result is minimal.

tests.explanation: No one-digit number can be fair; ten has one odd and one even digit.
No three-digit number is fair, and 1001 is the first fair four-digit number at least 403.
